pages.text: Swish, swish! Grandpa swept snow outside the shop. Under the roof edge, Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, pulled the blanket over the head. "Just a little longer..."
Nono tapped the window. "Gugu, you said you would pull the awning rope today!" "Yes, I will..." Gugu mumbled, then snored again.
When Gugu finally woke, the shop awning was already up. "Already?" Gugu pouted.
Grandpa stood the broom upright. "When you wake, stretch first. Then getting up is easy." Gugu rubbed sleepy eyes.
Gugu stretched both arms high, then both legs. The heavy body felt light, and the eyes opened wide. "Stretching chased the sleep away!"
Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, jingled the bell. "Sweeping sounds mean morning. Time to open your eyes." "Hear the sweep? Stretch!"
Gugu stepped into the alley and spread both arms. "Hello, morning alley!" The broom had left a neat, straight path.
Last, a face wash! Grandpa had put stove-warmed water in the bucket. Steam rose. A splash of warm water left Gugu wide awake.
Now Gugu knew the morning order. "One, hear the sweep? Stretch! Two, go out and say good morning! Three, wash your face with warm water!" Nono copied.
Next morning, Gugu came out at the sweeping sound and heaved up the awning. Grandpa patted Gugu's shoulder. Stretching chases sleep away. Gugu touched the green bag strap. "Hear the sweep? Stretch!"
